primitives.name: add
primitives.description: Adds two numbers and produces a result. The numbers must have type float or int and the result will be float or int type.
primitives.syntax_line: add [addend1] and [addend2] and store result in [addResult]

id_1.description: Addend1 must be a whole number or float

invalidValues.description: A string is provided as addend1

id_2.description: Addend2 must be a whole number or float

A value of zero is provided as the divisor

primitives.name: equal
primitives.description: Checks for equality between two participants and stores result in result
primitives._note: The python equality operator will not throw for default types but it can evaluate incorrectly in some cases (floating point precision (0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3 is false), comparing NaN values returns false). So this should be included in the meaning of the primitive so that the engine can reason about it. Also, if a participant is an object that has its __eq__ method written incorrectly, it can also throw an error. However, this can also be reasoned about by the engine if the meaning of the participant is established. So I will expand the invariants soon and I am leaving a note here track my thoughts.

primitives.name: terminal_input
primitives.description: Accepts and stores the input from terminal. This is a legacy primitive because the meaning stops at this layer (even though it is built from more primitives) but I am establishing it as a primitive because I haven't yet constructed this meaning from computable semantic primitives.
primitives.syntax_line: accept terminal input and store in [input]
primitives.syntax_extended: accept input and store in [input]. If EOF is reached without data, then [eof_behavior]. If keyboard interrupt is triggered, then [keyboard_behavior]
primitives._note: This primitive throws an EOFError and Keyboard Interrupt error. EOFError can be triggered by using CTRL+D in unix environments and Ctrl+Z followed by Enter in windows. Keyboard interrupts happen when Ctrl + C is used to terminate program in console. The meaning of these errors are built into the primitive and as part of the narrative that uses them the relevant behavior that should be exhibited can be specified. So in the synthesized implementation, I will throw the errors and then the specified meaning is used.
primitives._note2: I will extend the syntax for the errors and update the syntax_line after I implement the necessary functionality.

primitives.name: display_terminal
primitives.description: Displays the provided text in the console.
primitives._note: The implementation will throw if message combines multiple types. I have not exhausted all the possible issues and I'm leaving this note to revisit this and also specify the invariants.
